summary.intent: Get PR #400 (react families / checker lane) green and merged in order (#398, #400, #401), then resolve the merge conflict on the feat/gate-harness branch (#401).
summary.outcome: #400's checks went green (Checker lane fixed by updating expectations only) and #398 and #400 merged. #401 conflicts with main only in `justfile`, and a worker was dispatched to merge main into the branch, but its result has not yet been reported.

repo: The checker-lane expectations live in `apps/oracle/construct-suite/checker-expectations.json`; react rows record a verdict (identical/spelled vs less precise) plus a gap reason.
`just test-checker-lane` reproduces the Checker lane CI job locally; tsrs comes from `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (pinned @tsrs/darwin-arm64 0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta).
The comparator in `oracle-compare.ts` has an 'intersection Caliper left as written' rule that scores an intersection with an Omit family against a flat golden object as `less precise`.
`PropType` has no bigint primitive kind, so `bigint` serializes as `named "bigint"`; adding one changes the serialized shape.
The repo's lint gate is run via `just lint doc-check machete typos`.
Merge policy for this work: signed merge commits from main, no rebase, plain pushes.

code.finding: react/13 now `spelled` (gap removed); react/34, react/29 and react/07 stay `less precise` with corrected gap reasons.
The intersection rule marks `{color?, as?} & Omit<htmlAttributes div, "color">` as `less precise` against the golden's flat 279-member object. This is a comparator limitation, not a converter bug.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output and need independent verification; the assistant re-checked CI status itself via `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` instead of trusting the report's partial read.
`git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only` previews merge conflicts without touching the working tree.
Delegating mechanical conflict resolution to a worker with explicit constraints (signed merge commit, no rebase, run just --list/lint/cargo check) keeps the main session free.

friction: The first Checker-lane fix misjudged react/34 as a regression; it was actually a better type scored poorly by the comparator.
At hand-back time, Test / Rust, Test / Construct suite and Entire Gates were still in progress, so a follow-up poll was needed.
#401 picked up a `justfile` conflict after #398 and #400 merged.
open_items: Teach the comparator that an intersection with an Omit family equals the flattened object (for the no-regression gate and S8).
Add a bigint primitive kind to `PropType`, which changes the serialized shape.
Confirm the worker's merge of main into `feat/gate-harness` succeeded and that #401 reads MERGEABLE.
#396 still needs a look before merging.
The oracle was not run after the expectations change.
